title: Give every exposed frontend journey a RESP browser spec

values: journey declared, changed or evaluated in the plan with an exposed entrypoint
journey entrypoint exposure or surfaces changed
browser spec or `// Journey:` binding added/removed/renamed
facts.note: Primary activation. Needs a semantic plan/journey observer that reads each journey's entrypoint exposure and `surfaces` (wherever the declaration lives, not by filename), plus a spec-binding observer that maps `// Journey:` markers and RESP test URNs across all test files. Fires for plan-only changes and for pre-existing uncovered journeys, not only when specs are edited.

values: htmx_e2e_detector: exposed frontend journey without a bound RESP browser spec
facts.note: Detector finding from the htmx_e2e_detector validator; it must evaluate all in-scope journeys against all remaining qualifying specs.

Non-exhaustive hint only: matching a path is observable, but plan/journey declarations and misnamed marker-bearing test files can have arbitrary names, so globs neither define scope nor exhaustively locate inputs. node_modules, dist, build and _generated are excluded.
Hint only: task wording signals journey or responsive work; scope is still decided by entrypoint exposure and surfaces.

fires: The plan (even in a plan-only change) declares a journey with an exposed entrypoint and surfaces including frontend, and no test file anywhere carries `// Journey: <id>` with a RESP test URN for it.
An existing exposed journey that declares no surfaces has no bound RESP browser spec, even though no spec was edited in this change.
A RESP spec for an exposed frontend journey is deleted or its `// Journey:` binding is removed, and no other qualifying RESP spec remains bound to that journey.

For an exposed frontend journey, the only bound RESP spec is a misnamed test file (not *.e2e.ts) whose header comments carry a journey marker; it is judged as a browser spec and counts (or fails) as that journey's coverage.
doesNotFire: An exposed journey whose entrypoint surfaces exclude frontend.
Files under node_modules, dist, build or _generated.
A RESP spec is deleted but another qualifying RESP browser spec remains bound to the same journey.
A test file is recognised as a browser spec but is not bound to any in-scope (exposed, frontend-surfaced) journey; spec classification alone is not this rule's scope.

given: A journey whose entrypoint is exposed and whose `surfaces` include `frontend` (or declare none) exists in the plan
when: the journey set is declared, changed or evaluated (including plan-only changes and already-declared journeys)
then: That journey MUST have a journey spec (browser spec) bound to it by `// Journey: <journey id>` carrying a RESP test URN.
prefer: Add the RESP spec as soon as the plan declares a new exposed frontend journey.
avoid: Counting a unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string as RESP coverage.
Assuming a misnamed spec escapes judgement: any test file with a journey marker in its header comments is judged as a browser spec.
Writing RESP specs for internal journeys or journeys whose surfaces exclude frontend just to raise coverage.
unless: The journey is internal, or its exposed entrypoint `surfaces` exclude `frontend` — there is no screen to fit, so it is out of scope.
Vendored and generated trees (`node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `_generated`) are never scanned.
why: Every screen a user can reach should be proven to fit from mobile to desktop; exposed journeys are exactly those screens, and new ones appear here as soon as the plan declares them.
evidence: For each exposed journey with surfaces including frontend (or none declared), a browser spec exists whose header has `// Journey: <journey id>` and a RESP test URN.
htmx_e2e_detector reports no uncovered exposed journey.
verifier_detail: browser_spec = a `*.e2e.ts` file run by Playwright, OR any test file whose header comments carry a journey marker (`// Train:`, `// Journey:`, `// URN: test:train:…`, `// URN: test:journey:…`), so a misnamed one is still judged.
A unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string is not a browser_spec.

Scope: journeys with exposed entrypoint whose `surfaces` include `frontend` or declare no surfaces; skip internal journeys and those whose surfaces exclude frontend. Evaluate every in-scope journey, not only those touched by the change; a journey is covered if any qualifying bound RESP spec remains.
audit: New in the Bun/htmx browser tester, strict.
Summary: Every exposed journey has a RESP browser spec.
